claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard BLS12-381 G1 generator P0, recover x, the parallel batched Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md (P=262144 walks sharing one r=64 transition table with full-size uniform multipliers and starts and wrapping residues, Montgomery-batched additions, shared distinguished-point table) succeeds with probability at least 0.3995 using at most 2^127.69 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^106.0 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^24 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, or random-oracle premises. Success relies on the supported posited exploration law (pooled birthday with conservative merge factor, per-point labels, mixing degeneracy; no hash heuristic), the only heuristic, disclosed and supported in proof.md; degeneracy is a quantified (<= 1/q + 2^-100) heuristic event. This is an analytic best-known-attack cost analysis, not a claim of novelty or practical execution. The attack reads A_1=[s]P0 and runs rho on it; W(n) is constant in n.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical multi-walk attack path on the fixed prime-order toy curve (n=9883) and measure success rate against the birthday prediction. This does not establish production curve behavior or cost bounds.

title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: parallel batched rho, r=64, standard-regime wrapping walk, at 39%+ success
